clue.text: Before onset of Christmas, hear unorthodox one giving sermon

parts.note: the prefix pre- means before

indicators.note: unorthodox means irregular, so these letters are not kept in their usual order
the onset of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Ahead of the Christmas season, listen to an unconventional vicar delivering his sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' rearranges C (the onset of Christmas) with HEAR to give ACHER, which follows PRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister who delivers sermons from the pulpit is the classic sermon-giver.

clue.text: Departed after sanctimonious NT character

indicators.note: after places the word for departed behind the word for sanctimonious

parts.note: pi is informal British for piously self-righteous
late means departed, dead

explanation.surface: A pious New Testament figure who has died.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor of Judaea, appears in the New Testament Gospels.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman prefect who tried Jesus is a figure in the New Testament, abbreviated NT.

clue.text: Have people round for Christmas cheer?

definitions.text: Have people round for Christmas cheer?

parts.words: Have people round for Christmas cheer?
parts.note: hosting guests at your home over the festive season, and also amusing or cheering them, which this verb covers in both senses

explanation.surface: Inviting guests over for festive merriment.
explanation.definitionFit: To host guests at home is to receive them hospitably; the verb also means to amuse.

clue.text: Smart class choir burst into seasonal songs

indicators.note: burst suggests the words break apart so their letters can be reassembled

explanation.surface: A stylish school choir launches into festive music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst' shuffles all fifteen letters of SMART CLASS CHOIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Carols sung at Yuletide are songs of the festive season.

clue.text: Use English one in opening to Xmas story

indicators.note: the opening to a word is its first letter
in puts the numeral inside the word for story

parts.note: a plot is the story of a novel or play
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A suggestion to employ an English character at the start of a Christmas tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places I inside PLOT to make PLOIT, after E and X.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something is to make use of it, often to your own advantage.

clue.text: Notice associated with opening for the season preceding Christmas

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
a vent is an opening that lets air out

explanation.surface: A notice tied to the start of the run-up to Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The church season of four weeks before Christmas Day carries this name.

clue.text: One involved in pantomime turn again?

definitions.text: One involved in pantomime turn again?

parts.words: One involved in pantomime turn again?
parts.note: the hero of a famous British Christmas pantomime, who heard Bow Bells chime 'Turn again' and went back to London to become Lord Mayor

explanation.surface: A performer who keeps coming back in a festive show.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show for families; in this legend, Bow Bells call the hero back with 'Turn again'.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary poor boy turned Lord Mayor is a stock pantomime title role, recalled by the bells' words.

clue.text: Happening, still the ultimate for Baptist

parts.note: still and even both intensify a comparison (still better, even better)

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of a word is its last

explanation.surface: An occasion that is still the final word for John the Baptist.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is something that takes place, an occurrence.

clue.text: Teaching out abroad, phone after end of feast

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
abroad suggests going astray, so these letters are scattered

parts.note: to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: Giving lessons overseas, then calling home when the banquet ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges OUT into UTO, between T (end of feast) and RING.
explanation.definitionFit: Coaching a pupil privately is a form of instruction.

clue.text: Graduate leaving Basel party with piece of mistletoe? Scarcely

indicators.note: leaving means these letters go out of the city name

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
a do is a party

indicators.note: a piece of a word here is its first letter

explanation.surface: A graduate quits a Swiss party carrying a sprig of mistletoe, though hardly ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes BA from BASEL, leaving SEL; then DO and M follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely and hardly ever are synonyms of this adverb.

clue.text: Following behind first of reindeers

parts.note: behind means late, as in behind schedule

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Trailing behind the lead reindeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that comes afterwards follows in time.

clue.text: Foreseeing most original of children, I must have gift brought over

indicators.note: the gift is brought over the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a present is a gift

indicators.note: the most original letter of a word is its first

explanation.surface: Predicting what the most inventive child wants: I must have a present delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most original of' gives C; 'brought over' wraps PRESENT round CI.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prescient means knowing events before they happen.

clue.text: The Lord's House originally modelled in church doorway

indicators.note: modelled means shaped anew, so these letters are reformed

parts.note: here the possessive's S counts as a letter

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter

explanation.surface: The Lord's House first takes shape in the entrance to a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modelled' rearranges THE, LORDS and H (originally House).
explanation.definitionFit: The sill or entrance of a building's door is the threshold.

clue.text: Restaurant worker spilling one's drink (non-festive)

indicators.note: spilling means letting this letter fall out

parts.note: a waiter works in a restaurant
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A waiter knocks over someone's glass, the soft drink rather than the punch.
explanation.walkthrough: '(non-festive)' nudges away from wine or eggnog towards the plainest drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The clear liquid from the tap is the most basic beverage.

clue.text: Rodent Mother Mary initially spotted in garbage

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: in places the initial inside the word for garbage

parts.note: rot is nonsense or garbage

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter

explanation.surface: Mum's Mary spotted a rat in the rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts M inside ROT, giving RMOT after MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmot is a burrowing ground squirrel, a rodent of mountain regions.

clue.text: Old lady on the Italian island, one delivering Christmas cards?

parts.note: ma, mother, is informally the old lady
il is Italian for the
the Isle of Man is an island

explanation.surface: Mum goes on holiday to an island off Italy, one sending festive greetings.
explanation.definitionFit: A postman brings the seasonal cards to the door.

clue.text: Cocktail — small measure upset over a girl

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a gram is a small measure of weight
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A drink spilled over a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns GRAM into MARG.
explanation.definitionFit: Tequila mixed with lime and orange liqueur makes this classic cocktail.

clue.text: Most especially, a delivery involving love and, afterwards, extremes of vie lence

indicators.note: involving means the delivery wraps round these letters

parts.note: in cricket a ball is a single delivery by the bowler
love is zero in tennis, written O

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Above all, a delivery that brings love and then a little violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts O then VE (first and last letters of violence) inside BALL, giving BOVEALL after A.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means more than anything else, chiefly.

clue.text: Blessing one disciple on mountain

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain
I is the Roman numeral for one
son can mean a follower or disciple, as in the biblical sons of the prophets

explanation.surface: A single apostle offers a blessing from the mount.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down-the-page sense 'on' puts the mountain first: BEN, I, SON.
explanation.definitionFit: A benison is an old literary word for a benediction.

clue.text: Nobleman's seen in new year, just about

indicators.note: in places the nobleman between the abbreviations

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A peer appears at the New Year celebrations, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost and nearly both mean not quite but close to.

clue.text: Wise men initially meeting at ancient city to the east

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
E abbreviates east

explanation.surface: The Magi first meet at an old city in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise men' looks like the Magi but 'Wise' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mature people are sensible and experienced, showing good judgment.

clue.text: Tax collector that we converted after mass

indicators.note: after puts the converted letters behind the symbol for mass

parts.note: M is the symbol for mass in physics

indicators.note: converted means changed into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tax collector who changed his ways after attending a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges THAT WE into ATTHEW. The apostle was a tax collector before following Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gospel says the apostle was a publican, a collector of taxes, before his call.

clue.text: Figure of importance, but not character central to charade

indicators.note: but not means leaving out the given letter

parts.note: stature means standing or importance

indicators.note: the central letter of a seven-letter word is its fourth

explanation.surface: A significant figure, though not the star of a party game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central to charade' gives R; 'but not' removes it from STATURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculpted likeness of a person is a figure.

clue.text: Goddess in unimpressive stable

indicators.note: in shows the word lies within these words

explanation.surface: A deity in a plain cowshed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman goddess of the hearth is named Vesta.

clue.text: Birth heralded by celestial body above roof of this

indicators.note: in a down clue above puts the star over the next letter

parts.note: a star is a celestial body

indicators.note: in a down clue the roof of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A nativity announced by the star above this stable roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A start is a beginning, as birth is the beginning of life.

clue.text: Servant provides a drop of table wine and crackers inside

indicators.note: a drop of a word is its first letter
inside puts the jumbled letters within the wine

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A footman lays out wine and festive crackers on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' turns AND into DAN; 'inside' puts it in TENT to give TENDANT, after A and T.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendant is a servant waiting on someone.

clue.text: Maidservant brings in a ring for religious leader

indicators.note: brings in means the maidservant contains these letters

parts.note: an ayah is a nursemaid or maidservant in India
to toll is to ring a bell

explanation.surface: A maid brings a ring to a cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: AYAH is an Anglo-Indian word for a nanny or maid.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayatollah is a senior Shiite Muslim cleric.

clue.text: Ass appearing round small bend

indicators.note: round means the fool goes around the small letter

parts.note: a twit is a fool or ass

explanation.surface: A donkey appears at a little corner.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist something is to bend or turn it.

clue.text: In heart of Bethlehem, a series of questions

indicators.note: the heart of a nine-letter word is its fifth letter

parts.note: a test is a set of questions

explanation.surface: At the centre of Bethlehem, a quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link but is the definition: in fashion means newest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in vogue is the newest fashion.

clue.text: Ballet in middle of Christ mas week? An excess

indicators.note: the middle of a nine-letter word is its fifth letter

parts.note: a lake is a surplus, as in the EU wine lake

explanation.surface: A ballet staged midway through Christmas week, perhaps one too many.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'lake' is a stockpile of surplus produce, as in the European wine lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's famous ballet is a classic of the stage.
